cards.explanation: The answer is strength. The writer says the LORD "…has clothed and armed Himself with strength." (Psalm 93:1) Notice he says clothed AND armed, so strength is both what He wears and what He carries. Friends, I can barely carry a tray of cookies without my mustache getting tangled.

The answer is moved. The writer says the world "…is firmly established; it cannot be moved." (Psalm 93:1) That's a sturdy world, friends. My bakery counter wobbles when I sneeze, and this verse is talking about something far steadier.
The answer is True. The writer says to the LORD, "Your throne was established long ago…" (Psalm 93:2) Verse 1 talked about Him, and now the writer says "Your." That's worth noticing, friends.

The answer is all of eternity. The writer tells the LORD, "You are from all eternity." (Psalm 93:2) That's not just old, friends. It's far bigger than anything I can compare it to, and I'm only a cookie stamper with a mustache.

The answer is floodwaters. The writer says, "The floodwaters have risen, O LORD…" (Psalm 93:3) Notice he's still speaking right to the LORD, friends. The water is getting noisy, and he says so plainly.

The answer is that the LORD is on high above the roar. The writer says, "Above the roar of many waters—the mighty breakers of the sea—the LORD on high is majestic." (Psalm 93:4) The loudest thing in the verse is the sea, and the writer still puts the LORD above it. Friends, I can't even out-shout my own oven timer.

The answer is False. The writer says to the LORD, "Your testimonies are fully confirmed…" (Psalm 93:5) Fully confirmed means there's nothing left waiting on proof. That's a solid thing to lean on, friends.

The answer is holiness. The writer says, "holiness adorns Your house, O LORD…" (Psalm 93:5) Holiness is what the writer names as the house's adornment, friends. My bakery gets sprinkles on the counter, and the writer names something better for His house.

The answer is for all the days to come. The writer says holiness adorns the LORD's house "…for all the days to come." (Psalm 93:5) That's no expiration date, friends. My cookies can't say the same, because they go stale by the weekend. It's a lovely way to end the psalm.
